Galatians 5:19-23 “The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity and debauchery; idolatry and witchcraft; hatred, discord, jealousy, fits of rage, selfish ambition, dissensions, factions and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. This scripture is as convicting as they come, but that’s why I enjoy it so much. We want our hearts to align with Gods will but that’s not simply doing what He wants, it’s being who He created you to be in the situations that He puts you in. When He created us in His image, it wasn’t physically but spiritually. His image is holy and righteous, so we are holy and righteous. Sin has tainted our view of ourselves and our own fleshly desires distract us from His will. Thankfully, Christ Jesus provided us freedom from the torment of sin and the bondage of our flesh. caption:
Women of Sparta Wednesday 💚

Meet Payton Conroy, a junior infielder for Michigan State Softball.

Payton has continued to develop as a reliable presence in the infield, appearing in 25 games with 22 starts during the 2025 season. She added home runs against Detroit Mercy and Notre Dame and set a career high with two stolen bases against Illinois.

As a freshman in 2024, she made an immediate impact, appearing in 35 games with 29 starts primarily at shortstop. Her season included her first career home run against UT Arlington and back-to-back multi-hit performances against Coastal Carolina and Yale.

Before MSU, Payton starred at Stuart W. Cramer High School, earning All-State, All-County, and All-Conference honors and finishing her prep career with 19 home runs and a .431 batting average.

Women of Sparta celebrates the dedication and growth that define Spartan athletes — and Payton’s journey continues to take shape!

Eliana America Kelly I am so proud of you. Watching you go through this pregnancy process and give birth to our baby boy has been the most beautiful thing I have ever gotten to witness. It has opened my eyes up and made me love you in a way that I never knew I could. 

To see how strong you have been through this season of life in the face of the most challenging thing I’ve ever seen is a testament to the mother and wife that you are. Through the highs and lows of pregnancy, birth, and postpartum your love and sacrifice for our family inspires me to hopefully one day be able to serve our family in even half the capacity that you do every single day. 

You have brought the most precious and priceless thing into our life, something that fills my heart with love in a way that I’ve never experienced it before. Getting to see you be a mama is something that I’ve wanted since I’ve known you and getting to see you live that out is even more special than I could have imagined. 

You are truly the definition of a God fearing wife and mother and you live that out on a daily basis. I feel beyond blessed and undeserving of what you do for our family. Baby Shiloh is the biggest blessing that we have ever had and getting to be his father is a feeling that I can’t even put into words and I really can’t express how thankful I am and how much love I have for you for making me a father. 

You are an amazing mother and wife and I can’t wait to continue to experience that as we grow up together and raise Shiloh. I love you to the moon and back 🤍

caption:
To my auntie Shonna, I love you so much. 

This is one of my favorite pictures of you, because it shows how beautiful and bright your smile was. It was filled with a type of comfort and happiness that was uniquely you.

I want to say thank you for everything. Thank you for supporting me. Thank you for loving me. Thank you for always being there for me. Thank you for all the hugs. Thank you for demonstrating your unwavering faith through everything. You inspired me everyday, even when I didn’t see you. There aren’t enough words to describe how much you changed my life. 

What I know now from you that the greatest demonstration of love comes from loving those who aren’t blood, like family. Your love for not only us, but many others, was one of a kind. It was vibrant and beautiful. Auntie Shonna you have truly changed my life for the better with that love. 

I’ll never forget being the flower girl at your wedding. I felt so special, and like I had the most important job in the world. I can still hear us laughing as I “trained” to make sure your aisle was perfect. It meant everything to me to be part of that day with you. If I could, I’d make you the flower girl at my wedding, just to bring it full circle. I know you would’ve loved that, and I would’ve loved having you by my side in that way.

Even though you never got to see me compete in college, I know that you were so happy for me that I get to live out my childhood dreams. I know you were so proud of me and would never let me forget that. I wish more than anything that you could’ve seen me, because I know you would’ve been the loudest in the crowd. I know how bad you wanted to be there. I want you to know that for the rest of my college career, I will have you in mind as I get ready for every practice, warm up, and salute. 
 
Lastly, I want to thank you for showing your love for Jesus. No matter what you always trusted God’s plan, even when it was hard. You fought your cancer with everything you had, and you won the battle, just in a different way. I know that now you are resting peacefully and in the arms of our Heavenly Father. I love you so much auntie Shonna.  I’ll see you later.❤️

caption:
🥇 Henry Carr won TWO Olympic gold medals in 1964. 

A few decades later his great cousin @reggie__sharpe hit a walk-off in the Little League World Series. 

And today Reggie is creating content as a D1 baseball player at Michigan State.

Here’s what we loved about our conversation with Reggie… 

We only have newspaper clippings of his cousin’s Olympic journey. But Reggie is now starting to document everything - the grind, the day to day, the failures and the small wins of college baseball.

What if Henry Carr had been doing “day in the life” content during his Olympic training? How cool would that be?

That’s exactly what Reggie is building now. 

A complete visual diary that his kids will be able to experience like they were right there in the dugout with him.

In this episode Reggie broke down:
👉 Why his “stupid” fruit roll-up video hit 1M views while technical hitting content barely cracked 5K

👉 The exact iPhone + CapCut workflow he uses to create his videos in between classes and playing college baseball

👉 Going from “the guy” in your town to sitting out the season as a redshirt freshman

👉 The confidence boost of knowing you come from a lineage of champions

From Olympic medals to Little League heroics to viral TikToks - this is more than just content creation. It’s documenting greatness in real-time.

🎧 New episode with Michigan State’s Reggie Sharpe is live now. Comment REGGIE and we will send you the link to check it out now.

caption:
Tommy Szczepanski 🤝 MLB Draft League

What a year it’s been for Tommy. Success is never linear and this is a prime example of how sometimes you need to take a step back in order to go two forward. 

Tom has thrown the ball really well in the draft league this summer. He has run his FB up to 95.5 🔥 and showed off his swing and miss SL (81-83 with -15H). He adds a cutter in the upper 80s as well as a CH & 4S. He has 6IP so far with 11K/2BB. Showing that he is a Pro Ready arm that continues to get sharper each time out. 

Tom came in person with us last summer after struggling with inconsistencies in his command/velo. A lot of Tommy’s issues stemmed from compression in his throwing pec/shoulder and then getting his body out of the patterns he compensated into due to that compression. 

We started to attack his upper half first, buying time for the arm to flip up and actually work through layback cleanly. From there, we focused on applying force into the ground and not letting the COM fall over the toes allowing him to rotate cleanly into foot-strike. 

Keep it rolling @tommy11szczepanski 📈. Let’s go 

#Develop #DraftLeague 
🔥📈⛽️⁉️

caption: I’ve had a hard time this past month finding the right words about this team and my injury. There’s been so many emotions that I found it easier to just hold my thoughts in silence. Now this exciting, inspiring, incredible rollercoaster of a Senior High volleyball season has come to a close and I wanted to share what I’ve been feeling. From my notes app a few weeks ago: “I hate not being able to end my high school career on my own terms. I hate that I will never wear a bronc jersey again. I hate that I won’t get to play with my sister ever again. I hate that I won’t be able to compete for a state title with my team. I hate this injury. I hate how unfair this is.” It’s been easy to get stuck in the pain of an ending that I didn’t get to plan or prepare for. Clearly a lot of my sadness had also turned into anger. However, the most important part to me is that I didn’t want this injury defining my career. How lucky am I to have played alongside my best friends and be coached by the most amazing staff for the past 4 years. The lesson I’m taking away is that this season was about more than volleyball. The people I got to be loved by and love back through the Bronc program mean more than any stats or trophy. The grit that this team showed at state was beyond inspiring. It shows the heart of our team, the connection that we have, and proved that Senior Volleyball is Built to Last. From the bottom of my heart, I wouldn’t have wanted my last season with anyone else. To my sister - I am more proud of you than you’ll ever know. I see myself in you and getting to watch you take the spotlight has been my biggest accomplishment. I love you. I am your biggest fan forever. The Ormsby name will not be leaving Senior High anytime soon. To Coach Bad Bear - You’ve made every girl in this program a better volleyball player, but most importantly, a better human. I love you so much. Thank you for being an advocate and a role model. To my best friends on this team and across the state - You are badass volleyball players and I’m so proud of you!!! Gratitude and pride is what I feel for the connections this sport has created. This 2024 team is a family. SO blessed to be a Bronc. #10out
